x: At the start the two Sheffield lads, Allen and Proctor, made a quick getaway and joined by Lloyd Johnson, set up a good pace. Lloyd however, did not last with them for long and soon began to drop back.
At the start of the race Sheffield received a serious blow in the disqualification of Proctor who joined in an extremely fast start with his team mates Allen and Hardy and our own Harry Churcher.

Proctor made the journey to London to walk as an individual, and right well did he upset all the sages by walking extremely fast in the early stages and maintaining practically the same speed throughout, eventually returning the fastest time ever for this event.
…triumph which they achieved after fighting hard for so many years; the splendid walking of the Sheffield boys Allen and Proctor, and finally, with greatest respect, the performance of T.…
The start was a fairly fast one with Proctor, Lloyd Johnson, Martineau and Clayton well up in the lead. Proctor soon went away taking advantage of the home ground and knowing the course well.
Thirteen teams comprising 97 walkers lined up for the start of a three-lap course, and immediately Rex Whitlock, Don Tunbridge and Proctor went to the front and set the pace.
